# An imported package's var is bound once when the program starts, so a read
# is of the one value and an assignment to it is an overwrite: the old value
# is released, and the last one at teardown. The interpreter used to refuse
# the assignment ("cannot assign to undefined variable") and re-evaluate the
# initializer at every read, allocating a value nothing released, which kept
# testdata/owned_imported_var.txtar a golden with no run beside it.

sngl test app.sngl
stdout '^--- PASS: /testReopens '
stdout '^ok   1 tests, 0 failures$'
! stdout 'leak'

-- app.sngl --
import p "./p"
import "sngl:test"

func testReopens(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(p.current() == 9)
    p.reopen(10)
    t.assert(p.current() == 10)
    t.assert(p.closed == [9])
}
-- p/p.sngl --
import macro "sngl:macro"

#[macro.owned(close)]
struct file {
    fd int
}

var closed list[int] = []

func close(f file) {
    closed.push(f.fd)
}

func open(fd int) => file{fd=fd}

var cache = open(9)

func reopen(fd int) {
    cache = open(fd)
}

func current() => cache.fd
